lessons.title: ج (jīm) — the letter that opens جی
lessons.gloss: jīm — the letter that opens جی

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ج and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ت and ٹ once each, and name them.
Now say جی ہاں (jī hā̃), "yes". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
ج — jīm, the sound j.
It opens جی (jī) in جی ہاں, "yes", from the first chapter. A hooked head, a deep bowl, and one dot below.
1. start here: place the dot below.
2. lift, then sweep left through the pointed hooked head.
3. without lifting, continue down and around the bowl — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 1.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, Te, mim, jim, che, and more diacritics, independent ج (jīm) handwriting animation and flat-head insight (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).

segments.instruction: at جی ہاں and point at ج (jīm) inside it
segments.source: [YOU LOOK: at **جی ہاں** and point at ج inside it]

segments.instruction: ج (jīm) three times, saying j as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: ج three times, saying *j* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: ٹ, then ج, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — ج? (jīm, j.) Which word did it come from? (جی ہاں, jī hā̃, "yes".)

lessons.title: ح (baṛī he) — the letter that opens حافظ
lessons.gloss: baṛī he — the letter that opens حافظ

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ح and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ٹ and ج (jīm) once each, and name them.
Now say حافظ (hāfiz), "guardian". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
ح — baṛī he, "big he", the sound h.

It opens حافظ (hāfiz), the second half of خدا حافظ. Urdu already has an h, ہ, which you write; this one came in with Arabic words and sounds the same. It is the hook-and-bowl skeleton of ج (jīm), with no dots.
1. start here: sweep left through the pointed hooked head.
2. continue down and around the deep bowl without lifting — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 0. The pen never leaves the paper.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, Sīn, shīn, baṛī he, nūn, and nūn-e ġhunna, independent ح handwriting animation and Baṛī he instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).

segments.instruction: ح (baṛī he) three times, saying h as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: ح three times, saying *h* as you finish each one]

segments.instruction: ج (jīm), then ح (baṛī he), from memory
segments.source: [YOU WRITE: ج, then ح, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — ح? (baṛī he, h.) Which word did it come from? (حافظ, hāfiz, "guardian".)

lessons.title: خ (khe) — the letter that opens خدا
lessons.gloss: khe — the letter that opens خدا

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: خ and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ج (jīm) and ح (baṛī he) once each, and name them.
Now say خدا (khudā), "God". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
خ — khe, a kh scraped at the back of the throat.
It opens خدا (khudā), the first half of خدا حافظ. The same skeleton as ح (baṛī he), with one dot above.
1. start here: draw the short upper head from left to right.
2. without lifting, continue down and around the deep bowl.
3. lift once, then place the dot above — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 1.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, Khe, ze, zāl, swād, and zwād, independent خ (khe) handwriting animation and Khe instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).

segments.source: [YOU TRACE: خ three times, saying *kh* as you finish each one]

segments.instruction: ح (baṛī he), then خ (khe), from memory
segments.source: [YOU WRITE: ح, then خ, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — خ? (khe, kh.) Which word did it come from? (خدا, khudā, "God".)

your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: چ and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ح (baṛī he) and خ (khe) once each, and name them.
Now say سوچنا (sochnā), "to think". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
چ — che, the sound ch.
It is inside سوچنا (sochnā), "to think". The same skeleton once more, with three dots below: one letter, four sounds, and the dots decide which.
1. start here: sweep left through the pointed hooked head.
2. continue down and around the bowl without lifting.
3. after one lift, place the lower-left dot.
4. after another lift, place the lower-right dot.
5. after a third lift, place the lower-center dot — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 3.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, Te, mīm, jīm, che, and more diacritics, independent چ calligraphic and handwriting animations and Che instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).

segments.instruction: at سوچنا and point at چ (che) inside it
segments.source: [YOU LOOK: at **سوچنا** and point at چ inside it]

segments.instruction: چ (che) three times, saying ch as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: چ three times, saying *ch* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: خ, then چ, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — چ? (che, ch.) Which word did it come from? (سوچنا, sochnā, "to think".)
